Key asks: listing copy + assets, architecture diagram for VPC/on-prem connectivity, and security checklist review.
transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-03-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes | Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Sofia Lopez (CloudBridge PM), Daniel Zhang (Integration Eng), Rita Kumar (Solutions Architect)

[00:00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Priya and me from Redwood, and from CloudBridge Sofia, Daniel, and Rita. OK?
[00:00:10] Sofia Lopez: Yep, all good here.
[00:00:15] Priya Desai: Hi all, Priya here, I'll be driving the tech bits.
[00:00:20] Daniel Zhang: Daniel here, ready.
[00:00:25] Alex Kim: Cool. Agenda: marketplace listing checklist, reference arch for the joint solution, deployment artifacts (Helm/containers), and security questions. We'll leave 10 minutes for open Q/A. Sound good?
[00:00:35] Sofia Lopez: Sounds great.
[00:00:40] Priya Desai: Quick note, I'll call out where we typically see gaps when partners onboard — like role-based access and KMS key ownership.

[00:01:05] Alex Kim: To start, here's the marketplace flow: we need a partner listing page, short + long descriptions, logo (svg/png), screenshots, and a tech validation checklist. We'll share the checklist after this call. [link: marketplace-checklist]
[00:01:30] Sofia Lopez: For the listing copy, do you have word limits? We want to keep it consistent with our other marketplace entries.
[00:01:40] Alex Kim: Typical is 250 char short blurb and up to 1,000 for the long form; we'll include CTA guidelines in the doc. Also need a contact email and support SLA to display.
[00:01:55] Rita Kumar: On the support SLA, CloudBridge is proposing marketplace-managed support for initial stage, then co-supported later. Any Redwood constraints?
[00:02:05] Alex Kim: That's fine. We just need a clear escalation path in the listing and who owns what per severity. We'll put a template.

[00:02:30] Priya Desai: Moving to reference architecture: there are two main integration patterns partners use with Redwood — "hosted integration" where calls route to Redwood Hosted API, and "private integration" where Redwood Private runs in partner VPC or on-prem.
[00:02:45] Daniel Zhang: For CloudBridge's marketplace offering we intend to offer a self-hosted appliance in customer accounts (VPC) using our managed terraform and EKS modules. We need to confirm network requirements, egress rules, and any service endpoints.
[00:03:05] Priya Desai: Right, so for VPC deployments we usually require outbound HTTPS to specific Redwood control plane endpoints, and optional peering for metrics/telemetry. If you're doing on-prem we support an air-gapped bundle but that needs legal and additional security review.
[00:03:25] Sofia Lopez: What's the typical KV cache memory footprint? Our customers are sensitive about peak mem usage.
[00:03:30] Priya Desai: Depends on model and sequence length. Ballpark for a 20B variant it's a few GB per worker for KV cache, but you'll want to size nodes for headroom. Note: sometimes the transcription tools here say KV "cash" which is obviously wrong in docs.
[00:03:45] Daniel Zhang: Got it, we'll size conservatively.

[00:04:10] Alex Kim: On the artifacts side, we ask partners to provide a deployable Helm chart or operator with a sample values file and an image repo for the CloudBridge distribution. We can accept images hosted in partner ECR/GCR with a pull role.
[00:04:30] Rita Kumar: We prefer to publish a reference helm + operator. Any restrictions on base images?
[00:04:35] Priya Desai: No strict restrictions but we recommend distroless or slim images and not embedding keys. Also provide an init script for KMS integration if you need Redwood-managed keys vs customer keys.
[00:04:50] Daniel Zhang: About KMS, are you expecting partners to manage CMEK or can Redwood manage keys for the listing?
[00:04:55] Alex Kim: We support both. For marketplace listings many customers prefer customer-managed keys (CMEK) for compliance; we'll document the KMS integration patterns.

[00:05:20] Sofia Lopez: Security checklist — you mentioned SOC 2 artifacts and audit logs earlier. What's the minimum required for the marketplace?
[00:05:30] Priya Desai: Minimum is SOC 2 Type II or equivalent for production listings, SSO/SAML for partner console access, RBAC for operator roles, and audit logs export. For private deployments we'll also ask for KMS integration details and network isolation proofs.
[00:05:50] Alex Kim: We'll attach a short security questionnaire. [link: security-questionnaire]

[00:06:15] Daniel Zhang: Any restrictions on data residency? Some of our customers in EU insist data never leaves EU.
[00:06:20] Priya Desai: Redwood has region pins and private deployments in-region; for hosted we can pin region or recommend dedicated capacity in the desired region — we'll note that in the reference architecture.

[00:06:50] Alex Kim: Let's talk timelines: if CloudBridge can give assets quickly (logo, copy) and a basic helm chart, we can kick off a validation sandbox within two weeks. Full marketplace listing (including legal review) typically takes 4-6 weeks.
[00:07:10] Sofia Lopez: Two weeks to sandbox sounds good. We'll aim to have initial assets in 5 business days.

[00:07:30] Priya Desai: On the tech validation we'll run a simple end-to-end test: deploy the chart in a test VPC, validate connectivity to control plane endpoints, run a sample inference workload, and validate logs/metrics. We'll provide a validation checklist.
[00:07:50] Daniel Zhang: For the test workload, can you share a sample prompt set and expected telemetry we should capture?
[00:07:55] Priya Desai: Yes, will include prompt set and metric thresholds. Also note that the inference engine may behave differently when quantized; we'll note recommended quantization profiles but partner repo should include model variant notes.

[00:08:30] Alex Kim: A couple of commercial Qs — listing pricing structure: do you plan to surface Redwood-hosted billing, or will you handle billing and include Redwood as a component?
[00:08:40] Sofia Lopez: Likely CloudBridge will bill the customer and include Redwood as a component in our price. We'll need clear unit cost and recommended sizing to compute MSRP.
[00:08:55] Alex Kim: We'll share per-token / per-embedding unit estimates and typical throughput numbers for the supported variants. Note that numbers vary by hardware and quantization.

[00:09:20] Priya Desai: Now some nitty gritty: service accounts and credentials. For partner-hosted images we need a k8s service account with limited permissions — typically S3/GCS read for models, and secrets access only to mount KMS tokens. Avoid cluster-admin.
[00:09:40] Daniel Zhang: Understood. We'll scope least privilege.

[00:10:05] Rita Kumar: For network topology, do you support both NAT egress and VPC peering? Some customers prefer peering to avoid NAT costs.
[00:10:15] Priya Desai: We support both. Peering requires routes and sometimes IP ranges; we'll capture those in the checklist. NAT is fine for most customers.

[00:10:40] Alex Kim: Call out: please do not hardcode endpoints in the image — make them configurable through env vars or config maps. We've seen partners accidentally publish images with test endpoints.
[00:10:55] Daniel Zhang: Oof, yeah we'll audit that.

[00:11:20] Sofia Lopez: A quick question on monitoring: do you require Prometheus metrics format?
[00:11:25] Priya Desai: Prometheus exposition is preferred; we also support exporting to CloudWatch / Stackdriver if you include a metrics adapter. Provide metric names and labels in the doc.

[00:11:50] Alex Kim: On the go-to-market side: we'll collaborate on a co-branded listing, a joint blog post, and a short webinar. Marketing will loop in after the listing is validated.
[00:12:05] Sofia Lopez: Great. How about partner logos and tiering?
[00:12:10] Alex Kim: We'll include partner tier badges; provide logo in svg and png. Also provide a short customer success story if available.

[00:12:30] Priya Desai: Security follow-up: for on-prem / air-gapped we require a signed agreement and a checklist for patching and vulnerability management. That tends to take longer.
[00:12:45] Rita Kumar: We'll likely start with VPC deployments. Air-gapped could be future.

[00:13:10] Daniel Zhang: Any gotchas with IAM roles for cross-account pulls? We've seen ECR token expiry issues.
[00:13:15] Priya Desai: Use IRSA for EKS and a long-lived pull role or a token refresh mechanism. We'll include recommended patterns.

[00:13:40] Alex Kim: Let's run through a hypothetical checklist timeline: Day 0 assets provided, Day 3 Redwood validation, Day 7 sandbox deploy, Day 10 performance validation, Day 14 sign off for listing. That assumes no legal hurdles.
[00:14:00] Sofia Lopez: OK we'll aim to compress where possible.

[00:14:15] Priya Desai: One more thing: telemetry and error handling — include hooks for trace ids in requests so customers can cross-correlate logs.
[00:14:25] Daniel Zhang: We'll add trace id propagation.

[00:14:40] Alex Kim: Any other technical items?
[00:14:45] Rita Kumar: Just to confirm, do you provide a sandbox account or will CloudBridge need to create an eval account?
[00:14:50] Alex Kim: Redwood can stand up a sandbox for validation; we'll provide temporary credentials and endpoints.

[00:15:10] Priya Desai: Alright, let's capture next steps and owners...

[00:15:20] Alex Kim: Recap of agreed next steps: I will send the marketplace checklist and draft listing copy template; Daniel will send topology and sample helm chart; Priya will draft a reference architecture diagram and validation checklist. We'll schedule a follow-up the week of April 5th for a security/legal review.
[00:15:45] Sofia Lopez: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:15:50] Daniel Zhang: Thanks all.
[00:15:55] Rita Kumar: Thanks.

[00:16:10] Alex Kim: End of recording.

Notes: Transcript has some auto-caption errors (product names occasionally mis-typed like Redwood Dedicatd or KV "cash"). Shared artifacts: [link: marketplace-checklist], [link: security-questionnaire], [link: sample-values.yaml].
